title: Cold rebuild: make a pipeline fail when it should
summary: Fix a monitoring script with strict mode and a pipefail-safe count, from memory.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *Conditions, loops, functions and strict mode* you fixed a script whose pipeline hid
a failure. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are
exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; typing them cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: With **only** `set -e` (no pipefail), the script runs `curl -fsS http://bad.host/data | jq .count > count.txt`. curl fails (exit 6), jq succeeds on empty input. What happens?
options: The script continues: the pipeline's status is jq's (0)
bash refuses to run the pipeline
steps.explain: Without pipefail only the last command counts. With `-o pipefail` the pipeline returns 6 and `-e` stops the script.

steps.title: Make a pipeline fail when it should, cold
prompt: `~/jobs/count-errors.sh LOGFILE` writes the number of `ERROR` lines into `~/errors.txt`. Make it exit non-zero (without
printing `done`) when the log is missing, write `3` for `~/logs/app.log` and `0` for `~/logs/quiet.log` (both exit 0),
From memory: no hints this time.
